units.title: CLL Overview, Epidemiology, Defective Apoptosis Pathophysiology, Small Lymphocytic Leukemia (SLL) & Etiology
units.sec: CLL Overview, Epidemiology, Defective Apoptosis Pathophysiology, Small Lymphocytic Leukemia (SLL) & Etiology
units.guide:
Overview: CLL is the most common lymphoid leukemia (AML = m/c myeloid leukemia), Males > Females, low-grade; 80–85% asymptomatic/indolent, median age 72 yrs, median survival 10 yrs, 1–2% spontaneous regression.
Pathophysiology: Defective apoptosis of naive B-cells (CD19, CD20, CD21, CD22, CD79a, CD79b, S.IgM) → clonal expansion + acquire CD5, CD23 → monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis → CLL if lymphocytes >5000 cells/µL.
SLL & Etiology: SLL arises from memory B cell with identical immunophenotype/features and painless lymphadenopathy ± splenomegaly; CLL has strong familial inheritance and no risk with radiation.

units.sec: CLL Investigations, Smudge Cells, Richter Transformation, Warm AIHA, Staging Table & Indications for Treatment
units.guide:
Investigations: Unexplained lymphocytosis (~60,000–70,000; rarely normocytic normochromic anemia, thrombocytopenia); smear shows small blue round CLL lymphocytes (pale cytoplasm, no granules, moderate chromatin condensation) + Smudge cells; LN biopsy shows diffuse effacement (SLL).
High-risk indicators: (1) Richter transformation — low-grade (classically SLL) → high-grade (classically DLBCL) with ↑ lymphadenopathy & B symptoms (>10% weight loss in 6 mo, fever >100.4°F, ↑↑ LDH, ↑ PET nodal uptake); (2) Warm antibody AIHA (DAT/Coomb's test).
Staging & Rx indications: Stages 0 (lymphocytosis) & 1 (+ lymphadenopathy) = no treatment; Stages 2 (HSM), 3 (anemia), 4 (pancytopenia, as printed) = treatment required. Rx indications: Richter features, steroid-refractory AIHA, Stages 2–4 (massive splenomegaly, marrow failure).

units.title: CLL Prognostic Factors Table, FCR & BR Treatment Regimens, and Hairy Cell Leukemia Overview & Pathogenesis
units.sec: CLL Prognostic Factors Table, FCR & BR Treatment Regimens, and Hairy Cell Leukemia Overview & Pathogenesis
units.guide:
CLL prognosis & Rx: Good = hypermutated Ig heavy chain, chr 13q del; Bad = unmutated Ig heavy chain, other deletions (11q del, 17p del, trisomy 12), β2-microglobulin, ↑ LDH, Zap-70. Regimens: FCR (Fludarabine + Cyclophosphamide + Rituximab, TOC if fit); BR (Bendamustine + Rituximab, more commonly used).
Hairy Cell Leukemia: Rare low-grade B-cell neoplasm arising from memory B cell, >60 yrs (M > F). Pathogenesis: Memory B cell + BRAF mutation → Hairy cell → Spleen (massive splenomegaly) & Bone marrow (pancytopenia with neutropenia + monocytopenia, fibrosis → Aspergillosis, MAC, M. kansasii).

units.title: Hairy Cell Leukemia Investigations (Smear, Fried-Egg Marrow, Immunophenotype), Treatment & PAN Association
units.sec: Hairy Cell Leukemia Investigations (Smear, Fried-Egg Marrow, Immunophenotype), Treatment & PAN Association
units.guide:
Investigations: Smear shows mononuclear hairy cells (bilobed eccentric nuclei, hairy projections, low N:C ratio, abundant cytoplasm); marrow biopsy shows hairy cells, fibrosis & fried-egg / honeycomb appearance.
Immunophenotyping: Positive = CD19, CD20, CD22, CD11c, CD25, CD103, CD123, Annexin, TRAP (tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase); Negative = CD10, CD21.
Treatment & association: Purine nucleoside analogue (TOC) = Cladribine (DOC) > Pentostatin; BRAF inhibitor Vemurafenib (relapse); Rituximab (maintenance). Note: Polyarteritis nodosa is associated with hairy cell leukemia & hepatitis B.
